_source.title: Environmental Product Declaration — Lo-Carbon Sentinel Kinetic
_source._licence: Free public download, but NO redistribution licence is stated in the document and none was found for EPD Hub. The comparable programme operator (IBU) grants own-use only, expressly not sublicensable. This task is gitignored until that is resolved — see .gitignore and README.

_gold_provenance: Every figure below was read by eye off the rendered page (rendered at 2.4x with PyMuPDF and inspected visually), NOT taken from any parser's table extraction. This is deliberate and load-bearing: the candidate question sites were located using PyMuPDF's find_tables, so sourcing the gold the same way would make PyMuPDF-based solutions correct by construction and the benchmark would measure nothing. If these cases are ever revised, re-read the page — do not re-extract.

cases.label: Hazardous waste at A1
cases.question: In the table headed "End of life - waste", what value is given for "Hazardous waste" at life-cycle stage A1?
cases._why: First data column of the first table on the page. Its neighbour A2 is 3.84E-02, three orders away, so a one-column drift is obvious. This is the floor of the ladder: anything that reads the grid at all should get it.

cases.label: ADP-fossil resources at A1
cases.question: In the table of core environmental impact indicators (EN 15804+A2, EF 3.1), what is the A1 figure for "ADP-fossil resources"?
cases._why: Largest magnitude in its table, first data column. Included so the ladder has a rung a badly-degraded parser can still reach.

cases.label: Renewable PER as material at A3
cases.question: In the table headed "Use of natural resources", what value is recorded for "Renew. PER as material" at stage A3?
cases._why: The row is zero everywhere except A3 and its A1-A3 subtotal, so the target is the only non-zero cell in the first half of the row.

cases.label: GWP-biogenic at A3 (sign)
cases.question: In the table of core environmental impact indicators (EN 15804+A2, EF 3.1), what value is given for "GWP - biogenic" at stage A3? Include its sign.
cases._why: A3 on the row directly above (GWP - fossil) is +8.70E+00. A one-row drift returns a positive number, which the sign requirement catches.

cases.label: Non-hazardous waste at A5
cases.question: In the table headed "End of life - waste", what is the A5 figure for "Non-hazardous waste"?
cases._why: A4 on the same row is 7.02E-01. Reaching A5 means having survived six columns without drift.

cases.label: EP-marine at A4 (near-identical neighbour)
cases.question: In the table of core environmental impact indicators (EN 15804+A2, EF 3.1), what value does the A4 column give for "EP-marine"?
cases._why: A5 on the same row is 3.44E-03 — 4% away. A single-column drift produces a number that looks entirely plausible, so only an exact read passes. This is the failure pdf-inspector actually made on the previous case set, reproduced deliberately.

cases.label: Eutrophication at A3 under CML
cases.question: In the table of environmental impacts computed under EN 15804+A1, CML, what is the A3 figure for "Eutrophication"?
cases._why: Third data column of the third table on a page carrying three tables with identical column headers.

cases.label: Ionizing radiation A1-A3 subtotal
cases.question: In the table of additional (optional) environmental impact indicators, what figure appears in the A1-A3 column for "Ionizing radiation"?
cases._why: Requires picking the optional-indicators table over the core one on the previous page, which carries the same column headers.

cases.label: Acidification potential in the one populated B column
cases.question: In the table of core environmental impact indicators (EN 15804+A2, EF 3.1), almost every use-stage (B) column is reported as ND, and exactly one carries numbers. Which column is it, and what figure does it give for "Acidification potential"?
cases._why: The target sits eleven columns right of its row label with ten ND cells in between. A parser that collapses repeated ND cells loses the column alignment completely.

cases.label: ADP-fossil resources under module D
cases.question: In the table of core environmental impact indicators (EN 15804+A2, EF 3.1), what figure is reported for "ADP-fossil resources" under module D? Include its sign.
cases._why: Module D is the last of eighteen columns. Reaching it means the row survived every preceding column, including the ND run.

cases.label: Radioactive waste at C3 (both neighbours close)
cases.question: In the table headed "End of life - waste", what value is given for "Radioactive waste" at stage C3?
cases._why: C2 is 1.77E-06 and C4 is 1.51E-06 — a drift in either direction lands within a factor of three, well inside what looks like a plausible answer.

cases.label: Human toxicity cancer at B6 (extreme exponent)
cases.question: In the table of additional (optional) environmental impact indicators, what value is reported for "Human toxicity, cancer" in the B6 column?
cases._why: The smallest exponent in the document. A mangled exponent still looks like a number, so this catches silent corruption a magnitude-insensitive check would pass.

cases.label: POCP at C2 under CML
cases.question: In the table of environmental impacts computed under EN 15804+A1, CML, what is the C2 figure for the impact category "POCP"?
cases._why: Fourteen columns from the row label, in the third table on the page, and the EF 3.1 table on page 11 has a POCP row too with a different C2 value (2.95E-03). CEILING CASE: the no-parser control missed this one, answering 6.54E-04 — the C3 cell, one column right. The gold was re-verified afterwards by rendering the row at 4x and reading the cell again; C2 is 1.44E-04. The question is unambiguous and the gold is correct, so this measures the limit of reading a 19-column row at all. A parser solution that misses it should NOT be assumed to have failed because of its parser.

cases.label: Global Warming Potential A1-A3 under CML, not EF 3.1
cases.question: The document reports environmental impacts under two different standards in two separate tables. In the table of environmental impacts computed under EN 15804+A1, CML, what is the A1-A3 figure for "Global Warming Pot."?
cases._why: The EN 15804+A2 / EF 3.1 table on page 11 has a 'GWP - total' row whose A1-A3 is 2.94E+02. Both are global warming potential over the same modules for the same product; only the characterisation standard differs. A parser that merges the two tables, or a model that answers from the first one it finds, lands on 2.94E+02.

cases.label: Global Warming Potential module D under CML (0.8% decoy)
cases.question: In the table of environmental impacts computed under EN 15804+A1, CML, what figure is given for "Global Warming Pot." under module D? Include its sign.
cases._why: The EF 3.1 table's GWP - total module D is -2.47E+01 — 0.8% away. Answering from the wrong table produces a number that survives any tolerance loose enough to be forgiving, so the tolerance here is tightened to 0.2%. This is the hardest cell in the set and the one that most directly tests whether the two tables stayed separate.

cases.label: ADP-fossil A1 under CML
cases.question: In the table of environmental impacts computed under EN 15804+A1, CML, what is the A1 figure for "ADP-fossil"?
cases._why: Page 11's 'ADP-fossil resources' A1 is 4.66E+03 — same quantity, different standard, 8% apart. case_02 asks for that one deliberately, so a solution that confuses the tables cannot get both right.
cases._decoy: page 11 ADP-fossil resources A1 = 4.66E+03 (asked for in case_02)

cases.label: Non-renewable PER as energy at C3 (twin rows on one page)
cases.question: In the table headed "Use of natural resources", what value is given for "Non-re. PER as energy" at stage C3? Include its sign.
cases._why: The same page carries a second table with identical columns, and this table's rows come in confusable renewable/non-renewable pairs. 'Renew. PER as energy' at C3 is +5.36E-01 — a positive number three orders away.

cases.label: Which two rows sum to the exported-energy total
cases.question: In the table headed "End of life - output flows", the "Exported energy" row at stage A5 is the sum of two other rows in the same table at the same stage. Name those two rows and give the A5 figure for each.
cases.answer: Exported energy - Electricity (7.78E+00 MJ) and Exported energy - Heat (1.07E+01 MJ); they sum to 1.85E+01 MJ
cases._why: Needs three rows of one table read at the same column, then a check that they add up. A parser that merges rows or drops the zero-filled columns cannot supply the operands. Both component figures are required as `mode: any` because a correct answer naturally ends on the sum, not on either operand — the default last-wins rule scored the gold answer 0 until this was fixed. The two regex requirements stop a bare pair of numbers passing without the rows being identified.

cases.label: The one negative A1-A3 total
cases.question: Read down the A1-A3 column of the table of core environmental impact indicators (EN 15804+A2, EF 3.1). Exactly one impact category has a negative A1-A3 figure. Name it and give the figure.
cases._why: Requires one column read across all thirteen rows — the axis a row-by-row lineariser makes hardest. Scored on the value so that listing every GWP variant cannot pass.

cases.label: Footnote-driven unit conversion
cases.question: A footnote to the table of core environmental impact indicators (EN 15804+A2, EF 3.1) states that the EP-freshwater results are expressed in one unit and gives the factor needed to convert them to another. Apply that conversion to the EP-freshwater A1-A3 figure and state the converted value.
cases._why: Three things must survive parsing: the EP-freshwater row, the A1-A3 column, and the footnote below the table. The footnote writes the factor as '3,07' with a comma decimal separator, so reading it as 307 lands two orders of magnitude out.

_difficulty_model: Difficulty is assigned from STRUCTURAL properties that can be checked by eye on the rendered page — how many columns separate the cell from its row label, whether an adjacent cell is numerically close enough that a drift looks plausible (recorded per case in _decoy), whether a same-named row exists in another table, and whether the answer needs a scan or a combination rather than a point lookup. It is NOT taken from the text-preservation probes: one over-counts (a whole 19-column row fits inside its 220-character window) and the other under-counts (it assumes flat token output, but a markdown table lets the model read headers instead of counting positions), and neither predicted the one outcome measured.
